creator: Alexander Terp
description:
Landed on `rad-sprint`; carded after the fact so the sprint has a record of it.

rad had written the same snapshot harness five times: a kernel in `core/testing`, three suites each carrying their own copy of a walk-compare-rewrite loop, and a sixth minimal parser hand-rolled inside the formatter's structure test. go-snap is that kernel extracted into its own module, so roughly a thousand lines of parser, writer, update flags, diff rendering and file bookkeeping come out, replaced by four schema declarations and four runners.

Two things the module boundary buys:

- The formatter's structure test reads snapshots with the real parser. The `core/testing -> core -> rts/radfmt` cycle that forced the hand-roll does not exist across modules.
- Scripted-keystroke prompt testing comes from `go-snap/prompt` instead of a private copy of the same forty lines in `test_helpers.go`.

Each suite now declares its own sections, so a reader no longer meets a concrete syntax tree under STDOUT in a suite that never runs a process: the tree suite writes CST and AST, the checker CHECK, the formatter FORMATTED. A header naming a section its suite never declared is a parse error rather than content.

Two update paths worth knowing. `SNAP_UPDATE=<substr> go test ./...` reaches packages that never link go-snap and so would reject a `-update` flag. And an accepted update rewrites a file whenever canonical rendering differs from disk, not only when an expectation changed - which is how a format change migrates across every snapshot in one pass.

The port changes no expectation anywhere.
title: Retire rad's snapshot engine in favour of go-snap
